subject: Ingress topology proposal for AtlasBank pilot — brokered multipath tradeoffs
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Mike Santos <mike.santos@atlasbank.com>, atlasbank-netops@atlasbank.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-05T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Ingress topology proposal for AtlasBank pilot — brokered multipath tradeoffs

Mike / AtlasNetOps — attaching a short proposal and diagram for the pilot ingress topology. High level options we evaluated: VPC Peering (cross-account), vendor-managed PrivateLink endpoints, and a site-to-site (S2S) VPN with an ingress broker inside the Atlas VPC.

Quick summary:
- Peering: lowest latency and simplest packet path, but cross-account routing controls and central egress billing are constraints for your networking team. Works great for single-region high-throughput traffic.
- PrivateLink: best for strong cross-account isolation and per-service access controls. Adds a managed endpoint (interface ENI) on the customer side and avoids exposing our subnets; increases per-connection overhead and may introduce slightly higher p99 latency.
- S2S VPN + ingress broker: we propose a lightweight "broker agent" deployed as an autoscaling deployment in your VPC that terminates mTLS, performs path selection (peering/privatelink-like), and caches session/KV information to reduce cold-starts for model inference. This is the most operationally flexible and gives AtlasNetOps control over traffic shaping and egress policies, but requires an initial on-prem/VPC deployment and runbook.

I've attached the diagram (atlas-ingress-diagram.png) and a draft SOW (sow-draft.pdf). Please see the brief below for the operational tradeoffs and our recommended pilot: a brokered multipath approach with primary PrivateLink and S2S VPN fallback for cross-region resilience.

Can you confirm what the acceptable egress billing model is (Atlas pays egress vs Redwood pays)? That will affect which path we recommend as primary.

Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Mike Santos <mike.santos@atlasbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: atlasbank-netops@atlasbank.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-05T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ingress topology proposal for AtlasBank pilot — brokered multipath tradeoffs

Thanks Karthik — useful layout. A couple of quick clarifications from our side:

1) Security first: Atlas procurement will require that the primary path has zero public-facing IPs on our side and supports customer-managed KMS for any keys used within the VPC. Does PrivateLink satisfy that?
2) Billing: we prefer to keep visibility of egress (i.e., Atlas pays egress to Redwood) but need predictable monthly caps for budgeting.
3) Operational ownership: if we run a broker agent inside our VPC, what level of support do you provide for upgrades/incident response?

If PrivateLink gives us the zero-public-IP property and we can set a budgeted monthly cap, that feels attractive. But we want a fallback for cross-region incidents that doesn't rely on internet-exposed tunnels.

Mike
Sr. Cloud Network Engineer, AtlasBank

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mike Santos <mike.santos@atlasbank.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-06T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ingress topology proposal for AtlasBank pilot — brokered multipath tradeoffs

Mike — quick answers and a recommended operational model below.

PrivateLink and zero public IPs:
- Yes: PrivateLink creates interface endpoints in your subnets and traffic never traverses the public internet; no public IPs required on your side. It integrates with your SGs and NACLs and can be used with customer-managed KMS for any payload encryption keys we provision in coordination.

Billing/Visibility:
- PrivateLink traffic shows up as VPC endpoint traffic on your billing and flow logs; you can apply CloudWatch Metrics and set alarms against monthly egress. If you want Redwood to accept fixed-monthly egress billing, we can set a committed spend in the SOW.

Broker agent operational model (S2S + in-VPC agent):
- What we propose for the pilot: deploy our agent into a dedicated small-scale autoscaling group in a narrow set of subnets (control plane only). The agent terminates mutual TLS from our control plane, handles token exchange for per-request authentication, and acts as the local routing fabric for inference requests.
- Support: Redwood will run the agent as a managed artifact: we provide the container image, upgrade manifests, and a documented upgrade window. For the pilot, Level 2 on-call is included (patch windows + 24h incident triage) at no extra charge for the first quarter. After that, managed-support tiers are in the SOW.

Tradeoffs matrix (short):
- Latency: Peering ≈ best, PrivateLink ≈ +5–12ms p50/p95 overhead, Agent broker: depends on placement but can rival peering in-region.
- Throughput: Peering and PrivateLink both scale; PrivateLink ENI limits are a thing (we recommend multiple ENIs). Broker agent adds an extra hop but lets us do intelligent batching and prefix-caching to improve tokens/second economics.
- Security/segmentation: PrivateLink and broker give strongest segmentation. Peering needs strict route table controls to avoid lateral access.
- Failover: Broker + S2S VPN gives the most flexible failover patterns (we can route to alternate regions or fail to a hosted API path under your policy).

Recommendation for pilot: Primary PrivateLink interface endpoint per region, secondary S2S VPN to a broker agent for cross-region failover and local traffic shaping. This gives Atlas the zero-public-IP posture, clear billing visibility, and a deterministic fallback.

I've added a short appendix to the Drive link with ENI sizing recommendations and runbook checkpoints. If that model sounds acceptable, Karthik and I will produce a 2-week pilot plan and schedule a short runbook review with your NetOps.

- Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Mike Santos <mike.santos@atlasbank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-07T16:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ingress topology proposal for AtlasBank pilot — brokered multipath tradeoffs

Thanks all — summary and immediate next steps below.

Summary decision (pending your confirmation):
- Primary: PrivateLink interface endpoints in Primary-1 and Primary-2 AZs (per-region).
- Secondary: Managed S2S VPN to an in-VPC broker agent that we deploy into a dedicated subnet. VPN used only for failover and cross-region replication traffic; mainframe production traffic will prefer PrivateLink.
- Billing: Atlas to retain egress billing visibility; Redwood will accept a committed egress cap for the pilot quarter and include overage alerts.
- Security: Customer-managed KMS for at-rest keys in the VPC; agent will support mTLS + mutual attestation.

Immediate actions:
1) Atlas: confirm acceptance of egress committed cap and provide target cap number (reply by 2027-06-10).
2) Redwood (Marissa/Karthik): produce pilot SOW and 2-week runbook; share by 2027-06-11.
3) NetOps working session: schedule a 60m call to walk the diagram and ENI sizing (Atlas to propose times).

If Atlas agrees to the cap, we'll treat PrivateLink as primary for the pilot and implement the broker agent as a resilient fallback so incidents in a single region won't cause service loss.

Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
